transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve become convinced that an MBA classmate and a startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. Things they say in class, or messages on Slack, feel like coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. I know it sounds difficult to explain, but it feels very real to me.
Have you been using any alcohol, marijuana, stimulants, or other recreational drugs recently?
I’m not really sure what you’d count as relevant. I haven’t noticed anything like that affecting me.
Over the time you've had these beliefs, have you also noticed periods where your mood was unusually high, energetic, or irritable, or alternatively very low and depressed?

Most days I’ve felt really switched on and optimistic, like I’m right on the edge of something huge. But I’ve also been more irritable than usual—snapping at my teammates or my boyfriend over little delays that normally wouldn’t bother me.
How long have you been feeling this unusually high energy, optimism, and irritability—has it been going on for a week or more?
Yeah, it’s been about two months now—since I started the part-time MBA prerequisite program while still working my operations job.

Have you noticed these beliefs about your classmate and advisor coordinating things continuing even during times when your mood feels back to normal, or do they only come up when you're feeling unusually energetic or irritable?
They only started during this stretch. Before I got this energized and driven with the MBA program, I didn’t have things feeling coded or hear my name when nobody was there.
Have you ever had a period before this—lasting a week or more—where you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable, or on the other hand, deeply depressed, prior to starting the MBA program?
I don’t think so. Before the MBA program, I felt pretty normal overall—nothing like this that lasted a week or more.
Does anyone in your family—parents, siblings, or other close relatives—have a history of bipolar disorder, manic episodes, or severe mood swings?
I’m not really sure about that. I don’t know of anyone in my close family who’s had that kind of history.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a 2-month period of elevated mood, increased energy, grandiosity, decreased need for reassurance, and irritability, consistent with a manic episode. During this same period, she developed psychotic symptoms (delusions of reference/persecution regarding coordinated signaling from classmates/advisors, possibly auditory phenomena). These psychotic symptoms emerged only during the manic episode and were absent during euthymic periods, indicating mood-congruent/incongruent psychotic features occurring exclusively within a manic episode rather than an independent psychotic disorder. There is no prior history of mood episodes (ruling out bipolar disorder with recurrent episodes, F31.2) and no evidence of psychotic symptoms persisting outside mood episodes (ruling out schizoaffective disorder or primary psychotic disorder). No substance use or intoxication reported. This is a first single manic episode with psychotic symptoms, meeting criteria for F30.2.
